title: Confirm
description: Asks the user to confirm an action: a themed replacement for window.confirm. Use the declarative ConfirmDialog or await confirm() from anywhere; with a ConfirmProvider the dialog renders inside your app tree, without one a standalone host is mounted on demand, and on the server confirm() resolves false.

imperative.title: Imperative confirm()
imperative.description: await confirm({...}) resolves true when confirmed and false when cancelled (button, Escape or backdrop). No provider needed.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: color sets the tone of the confirm button: primary (default), warning, or danger for destructive actions (its label then defaults to "Delete"). The cancel button is always a neutral outline button.

provider.title: With ConfirmProvider
provider.description: useConfirm() returns the provider's confirm, so dialogs share your app's context. Concurrent requests are shown one at a time.

declarative.title: Declarative ConfirmDialog
declarative.description: Controlled dialog; loading shows a spinner and locks cancel while onConfirm runs.

ConfirmDialogProps.onOpenChange: Called with false when the user cancels (cancel button, close, Escape, backdrop click)
ConfirmDialogProps.onConfirm: Called when the confirm button is pressed; the dialog does not close by itself

ConfirmOptions.title: Title (the dialog's accessible name)
ConfirmOptions.confirmLabel: Label of the confirm button; defaults to "Confirm", or "Delete" for color="danger"
ConfirmOptions.cancelLabel: Label of the cancel button; defaults to the localized "Cancel"
ConfirmOptions.closeLabel: Accessible label of the close (×) button; defaults to the localized "Close"
ConfirmOptions.color: Semantic color of the confirm button: primary, warning or danger (destructive; defaults its label to "Delete")
ConfirmOptions.loading: Shows a spinner on the confirm button and disables cancel
ConfirmOptions.confirmDisabled: Natively disables the confirm button (removes it from the tab order); with loading alone it stays focusable but cannot be activated again

ConfirmProviderProps.children: Application subtree; useConfirm() / confirm() render their dialogs here
